using System;
using System.Collections.Generic;
using System.IO;
using System.Linq;

class Voxel {
    public int Mass;
    public int Value;
    public bool IsEmpty => Mass == 0;
}

class Program {
    static void Main() {
        string headerLine = Console.ReadLine();
        if (string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(headerLine)) {
            Console.WriteLine(0);
            return;
        }

        string[] headerParts = headerLine.Split(new[] { ' ' }, StringSplitOptions.RemoveEmptyEntries);
        if (headerParts.Length < 6) {
            Console.WriteLine(0);
            return;
        }

        int X = int.Parse(headerParts[0]);
        int Y = int.Parse(headerParts[1]);
        int Z = int.Parse(headerParts[2]);
        // Block sizes ignored for this implementation as we work in voxel units

        long totalVoxels = (long)X * Y * Z;
        int scaleThreshold = 250000; // ~63x63x63 or smaller for detailed strategy

        List<string> operations = new List<string>();

        if (totalVoxels > 20000000L) {
            // Large scale: focus only on immediate vicinity of (0,0) with greedy direct moves
            // Read and discard most input efficiently
            var stdin = Console.OpenStandardInput();
            byte[] discardBuffer = new byte[8192];
            long bytesToRead = totalVoxels;
            while (bytesToRead > 0) {
                int toRead = (int)Math.Min(discardBuffer.Length, bytesToRead);
                int read = stdin.Read(discardBuffer, 0, toRead);
                if (read == 0) break;
                bytesToRead -= read;
            }
            
            // Generate limited high-value moves near origin using simplified logic
            GenerateLargeScaleOperations(X, Y, Z, operations);
        } else {
            // Small/Medium scale: load data and use more detailed strategy
            Voxel[,,] world = new Voxel[X, Y, Z];
            var stdin = Console.OpenStandardInput();
            byte[] buffer = new byte[1];

            for (int x = 0; x < X; x++) {
                for (int y = 0; y < Y; y++) {
                    for (int z = 0; z < Z; z++) {
                        if (stdin.Read(buffer, 0, 1) == 0) {
                            // Fallback if input ends early
                            world[x, y, z] = new Voxel { Mass = 0, Value = 0 };
                            continue;
                        }
                        byte d = buffer[0];
                        world[x, y, z] = new Voxel {
                            Mass = d % 16,
                            Value = d / 16
                        };
                    }
                }
            }

            if (totalVoxels <= scaleThreshold) {
                // Detailed strategy: prioritize high value, find exposed, plan simple paths
                GenerateDetailedOperations(world, X, Y, Z, operations);
            } else {
                // Medium scale: greedy column mining toward origin
                GenerateMediumScaleOperations(world, X, Y, Z, operations);
            }
        }

        // Output
        Console.WriteLine(operations.Count);
        foreach (var op in operations) {
            Console.WriteLine(op);
        }
    }

    static void GenerateDetailedOperations(Voxel[,,] world, int X, int Y, int Z, List<string> operations) {
        // Simple detailed strategy: process highest value voxels first with direct Manhattan paths
        var valuableVoxels = new List<(int x, int y, int z, int value, int mass)>();

        for (int x = 0; x < X; x++) {
            for (int y = 0; y < Y; y++) {
                for (int z = 0; z < Z; z++) {
                    var v = world[x, y, z];
                    if (!v.IsEmpty && v.Value >= 8) { // Focus on valuable ore
                        valuableVoxels.Add((x, y, z, v.Value, v.Mass));
                    }
                }
            }
        }

        // Sort by value descending
        valuableVoxels.Sort((a, b) => b.value.CompareTo(a.value));

        int maxOps = Math.Min(valuableVoxels.Count, 500); // Limit for time

        for (int i = 0; i < maxOps; i++) {
            var (digX, digY, digZ, val, mass) = valuableVoxels[i];
            
            // Simple 4-connected path to (0,0) - assume flat for simplicity, adjust Z implicitly
            List<(int stepX, int stepY)> path = GenerateSimplePath(digX, digY, 0, 0);
            
            string op = $"{path.Count} {digX} {digY} {digZ}";
            foreach (var step in path) {
                op += $" {step.stepX} {step.stepY}";
            }
            op += " 0 0"; // destX destY (processing plant)

            operations.Add(op);
        }
    }

    static void GenerateMediumScaleOperations(Voxel[,,] world, int X, int Y, int Z, List<string> operations) {
        // Greedy: mine columns closest to origin first
        var columns = new List<(int x, int y, int totalValue)>();

        for (int x = 0; x < X; x++) {
            for (int y = 0; y < Y; y++) {
                int totalVal = 0;
                for (int z = 0; z < Z; z++) {
                    totalVal += world[x, y, z].Value;
                }
                if (totalVal > 0) {
                    columns.Add((x, y, totalVal));
                }
            }
        }

        columns.Sort((a, b) => {
            int distA = Math.Abs(a.x) + Math.Abs(a.y);
            int distB = Math.Abs(b.x) + Math.Abs(b.y);
            if (distA != distB) return distA.CompareTo(distB);
            return b.totalValue.CompareTo(a.totalValue);
        });

        int processed = 0;
        foreach (var col in columns.Take(200)) {
            // Mine from top down in column
            for (int z = Z - 1; z >= 0; z--) {
                var v = world[col.x, col.y, z];
                if (!v.IsEmpty && v.Value >= 5 && processed < 300) {
                    List<(int, int)> path = GenerateSimplePath(col.x, col.y, 0, 0);
                    
                    string op = $"{path.Count} {col.x} {col.y} {z}";
                    foreach (var p in path) {
                        op += $" {p.Item1} {p.Item2}";
                    }
                    op += " 0 0";

                    operations.Add(op);
                    processed++;
                }
            }
        }
    }

    static void GenerateLargeScaleOperations(int X, int Y, int Z, List<string> operations) {
        // Large scale adaptive: only process a small area around (0,0) with direct moves
        // Assume some valuable dirt exists near origin
        int maxRange = Math.Min(15, Math.Min(X, Y));
        
        for (int x = 0; x < maxRange; x++) {
            for (int y = 0; y < maxRange; y++) {
                if (x == 0 && y == 0) continue;
                
                // Simplified assumption: move "dirt" from these positions
                List<(int, int)> path = GenerateSimplePath(x, y, 0, 0);
                
                // Use mid Z as example dig level
                int digZ = Math.Min(20, Z / 2);
                
                string op = $"{path.Count} {x} {y} {digZ}";
                foreach (var p in path) {
                    op += $" {p.Item1} {p.Item2}";
                }
                op += " 0 0";

                operations.Add(op);
                
                if (operations.Count > 50) break;
            }
            if (operations.Count > 50) break;
        }
    }

    static List<(int stepX, int stepY)> GenerateSimplePath(int startX, int startY, int targetX, int targetY) {
        // Generate a simple 4-connected Manhattan path
        var path = new List<(int, int)>();
        int cx = startX;
        int cy = startY;

        while (cx != targetX || cy != targetY) {
            if (cx < targetX) {
                cx++;
                path.Add((1, 0)); // step right
            } else if (cx > targetX) {
                cx--;
                path.Add((-1, 0));
            } else if (cy < targetY) {
                cy++;
                path.Add((0, 1));
            } else if (cy > targetY) {
                cy--;
                path.Add((0, -1));
            }
            
            // Safety limit
            if (path.Count > 10000) break;
        }

        return path;
    }
}

use std::io::{self, BufRead};
use std::collections::HashMap;

#[derive(Clone)]
struct Sample {
    hole_id: String,
    idx: usize,
    x: f64,
    y: f64,
    z: f64,
    values: Vec<f64>,
}

#[derive(Clone)]
struct Outlier {
    hole_id: String,
    sample_idx: usize,
    property: String,
    confidence: f64,
}

fn main() {
    let stdin = io::stdin();
    let mut lines = stdin.lock().lines();
    
    // Parse header
    let first_line = match lines.next() {
        Some(Ok(line)) => line,
        _ => return,
    };
    let mut parts = first_line.split_whitespace();
    let num_holes: usize = parts.next().unwrap_or("0").parse().unwrap_or(0);
    let num_props: usize = parts.next().unwrap_or("0").parse().unwrap_or(0);
    
    // Parse property names
    let prop_line = match lines.next() {
        Some(Ok(line)) => line,
        _ => return,
    };
    let properties: Vec<String> = prop_line.split_whitespace().map(String::from).collect();
    
    // Parse holes and samples
    let mut all_samples: Vec<Sample> = Vec::new();
    let mut hole_map: HashMap<String, Vec<usize>> = HashMap::new();
    
    for _ in 0..num_holes {
        let line = match lines.next() {
            Some(Ok(line)) => line,
            _ => break,
        };
        let mut parts = line.split_whitespace();
        
        let hole_id = parts.next().unwrap_or("").to_string();
        if hole_id.is_empty() { continue; }
        
        let start_x: f64 = parts.next().unwrap_or("0").parse().unwrap_or(0.0);
        let start_y: f64 = parts.next().unwrap_or("0").parse().unwrap_or(0.0);
        let start_z: f64 = parts.next().unwrap_or("0").parse().unwrap_or(0.0);
        let dir_x: f64 = parts.next().unwrap_or("0").parse().unwrap_or(0.0);
        let dir_y: f64 = parts.next().unwrap_or("0").parse().unwrap_or(0.0);
        let dir_z: f64 = parts.next().unwrap_or("0").parse().unwrap_or(0.0);
        let length: f64 = parts.next().unwrap_or("1").parse().unwrap_or(1.0);
        let num_samples: usize = parts.next().unwrap_or("0").parse().unwrap_or(0);
        
        let dir_len = (dir_x * dir_x + dir_y * dir_y + dir_z * dir_z).sqrt();
        let (ux, uy, uz) = if dir_len > 1e-9 {
            (dir_x / dir_len, dir_y / dir_len, dir_z / dir_len)
        } else {
            (0.0, 0.0, 1.0)
        };
        
        let mut hole_indices = Vec::new();
        
        for i in 0..num_samples {
            let sample_line = match lines.next() {
                Some(Ok(line)) => line,
                _ => break,
            };
            let mut s_parts = sample_line.split_whitespace();
            
            let depth: f64 = match s_parts.next() {
                Some(d) => d.parse().unwrap_or(0.0),
                None => continue,
            };
            
            let mut values = Vec::with_capacity(num_props);
            for _ in 0..num_props {
                let v: f64 = s_parts.next().unwrap_or("0").parse().unwrap_or(0.0);
                values.push(v);
            }
            
            // Calculate 3D position
            let x = start_x + ux * depth;
            let y = start_y + uy * depth;
            let z = start_z + uz * depth;
            
            let sample = Sample {
                hole_id: hole_id.clone(),
                idx: i,
                x,
                y,
                z,
                values,
            };
            
            let sample_idx = all_samples.len();
            all_samples.push(sample);
            hole_indices.push(sample_idx);
        }
        
        if !hole_indices.is_empty() {
            hole_map.insert(hole_id, hole_indices);
        }
    }
    
    // Detect outliers with adaptive strategy
    let outliers = detect_outliers(&all_samples, &properties, &hole_map);
    
    // Output results
    println!("{}", outliers.len());
    for outlier in outliers {
        println!("{} {} {} {:.4}", 
            outlier.hole_id, outlier.sample_idx, outlier.property, outlier.confidence);
    }
}

fn detect_outliers(
    samples: &[Sample], 
    properties: &[String], 
    hole_map: &HashMap<String, Vec<usize>>
) -> Vec<Outlier> {
    let n = samples.len();
    let mut outliers = Vec::new();
    
    // Adaptive strategy based on dataset scale
    if n < 1500 {
        // Small dataset: brute force neighbor search
        detect_outliers_brute(samples, properties, &mut outliers);
    } else if n < 15000 {
        // Medium dataset: sampled neighbor search with hole context
        detect_outliers_sampled(samples, properties, hole_map, &mut outliers);
    } else {
        // Large dataset: hole-based continuity + limited spatial sampling
        detect_outliers_large(samples, properties, hole_map, &mut outliers);
    }
    
    // Deduplicate and keep highest confidence per (hole, sample, property)
    let mut best: HashMap<(String, usize, String), f64> = HashMap::new();
    for o in outliers {
        let key = (o.hole_id.clone(), o.sample_idx, o.property.clone());
        let entry = best.entry(key).or_insert(0.0);
        if o.confidence > *entry {
            *entry = o.confidence;
        }
    }
    
    let mut result: Vec<Outlier> = best.into_iter()
        .map(|((hole_id, sample_idx, property), confidence)| {
            Outlier { hole_id, sample_idx, property, confidence }
        })
        .collect();
    
    // Sort by confidence descending
    result.sort_by(|a, b| b.confidence.partial_cmp(&a.confidence).unwrap_or(std::cmp::Ordering::Equal));
    
    // Limit output for very large datasets
    if result.len() > 50000 {
        result.truncate(50000);
    }
    
    result
}

fn detect_outliers_brute(samples: &[Sample], properties: &[String], outliers: &mut Vec<Outlier>) {
    let n = samples.len();
    let k = 12;
    
    for i in 0..n {
        // Find k nearest neighbors
        let mut distances: Vec<(usize, f64)> = Vec::new();
        
        for j in 0..n {
            if i == j { continue; }
            let dx = samples[i].x - samples[j].x;
            let dy = samples[i].y - samples[j].y;
            let dz = samples[i].z - samples[j].z;
            let dist = (dx*dx + dy*dy + dz*dz).sqrt();
            distances.push((j, dist));
        }
        
        if distances.is_empty() { continue; }
        
        distances.sort_by(|a, b| a.1.partial_cmp(&b.1).unwrap());
        let neighbors: Vec<usize> = distances.iter().take(k).map(|&(idx, _)| idx).collect();
        
        for p in 0..properties.len() {
            let neighbor_values: Vec<f64> = neighbors.iter()
                .map(|&j| samples[j].values[p])
                .collect();
            
            let value = samples[i].values[p];
            let confidence = compute_confidence(value, &neighbor_values);
            
            if confidence > 2.0 {
                outliers.push(Outlier {
                    hole_id: samples[i].hole_id.clone(),
                    sample_idx: samples[i].idx,
                    property: properties[p].clone(),
                    confidence,
                });
            }
        }
    }
}

fn detect_outliers_sampled(
    samples: &[Sample], 
    properties: &[String], 
    hole_map: &HashMap<String, Vec<usize>>,
    outliers: &mut Vec<Outlier>
) {
    let n = samples.len();
    let sample_size = 80;
    let k = 10;
    
    for i in 0..n {
        let mut candidates = Vec::new();
        
        // Always include same-hole samples (strong spatial correlation)
        if let Some(hole_indices) = hole_map.get(&samples[i].hole_id) {
            for &j in hole_indices {
                if i != j {
                    candidates.push(j);
                }
            }
        }
        
        // Sample additional candidates using deterministic pseudo-random selection
        let mut offset = 1;
        while candidates.len() < sample_size && offset < n {
            let j = (i + offset * 31 + 17) % n;
            if i != j && !candidates.contains(&j) {
                candidates.push(j);
            }
            offset += 1;
        }
        
        // Calculate distances
        let mut distances: Vec<(usize, f64)> = candidates.iter()
            .map(|&j| {
                let dx = samples[i].x - samples[j].x;
                let dy = samples[i].y - samples[j].y;
                let dz = samples[i].z - samples[j].z;
                let dist = (dx*dx + dy*dy + dz*dz).sqrt();
                (j, dist)
            })
            .collect();
        
        distances.sort_by(|a, b| a.1.partial_cmp(&b.1).unwrap());
        let neighbors: Vec<usize> = distances.iter().take(k).map(|&(idx, _)| idx).collect();
        
        if neighbors.is_empty() { continue; }
        
        for p in 0..properties.len() {
            let neighbor_values: Vec<f64> = neighbors.iter()
                .map(|&j| samples[j].values[p])
                .collect();
            
            let value = samples[i].values[p];
            let confidence = compute_confidence(value, &neighbor_values);
            
            if confidence > 2.3 {
                outliers.push(Outlier {
                    hole_id: samples[i].hole_id.clone(),
                    sample_idx: samples[i].idx,
                    property: properties[p].clone(),
                    confidence,
                });
            }
        }
    }
}

fn detect_outliers_large(
    samples: &[Sample], 
    properties: &[String], 
    hole_map: &HashMap<String, Vec<usize>>,
    outliers: &mut Vec<Outlier>
) {
    // Pass 1: Within-hole continuity check (O(n) total)
    for (hole_id, indices) in hole_map {
        if indices.len() < 3 { continue; }
        
        for i in 1..indices.len()-1 {
            let prev = indices[i-1];
            let curr = indices[i];
            let next = indices[i+1];
            
            for p in 0..properties.len() {
                let prev_val = samples[prev].values[p];
                let curr_val = samples[curr].values[p];
                let next_val = samples[next].values[p];
                
                let expected = (prev_val + next_val) / 2.0;
                let deviation = (curr_val - expected).abs();
                let neighbor_dev = ((prev_val - expected).abs() + (next_val - expected).abs()) / 2.0;
                let scale = neighbor_dev + 0.001;
                
                let confidence = deviation / scale;
                
                if confidence > 3.5 {
                    outliers.push(Outlier {
                        hole_id: hole_id.clone(),
                        sample_idx: samples[curr].idx,
                        property: properties[p].clone(),
                        confidence,
                    });
                }
            }
        }
    }
    
    // Pass 2: Limited cross-hole spatial comparison
    let sample_size = 25;
    
    for i in (0..samples.len()).step_by(4) { // Sample every 4th point for speed
        let mut neighbors = Vec::new();
        
        // Get samples from other holes
        for offset in 0..sample_size {
            let j = (i * 37 + offset * 23) % samples.len();
            if samples[j].hole_id != samples[i].hole_id {
                neighbors.push(j);
            }
        }
        
        if neighbors.len() < 5 { continue; }
        
        for p in 0..properties.len() {
            let neighbor_values: Vec<f64> = neighbors.iter()
                .map(|&j| samples[j].values[p])
                .collect();
            
            let value = samples[i].values[p];
            let confidence = compute_confidence(value, &neighbor_values);
            
            if confidence > 4.0 {
                outliers.push(Outlier {
                    hole_id: samples[i].hole_id.clone(),
                    sample_idx: samples[i].idx,
                    property: properties[p].clone(),
                    confidence,
                });
            }
        }
    }
}

fn compute_confidence(value: f64, neighbors: &[f64]) -> f64 {
    if neighbors.is_empty() {
        return 0.0;
    }
    
    // Compute median
    let mut sorted = neighbors.to_vec();
    sorted.sort_by(|a, b| a.partial_cmp(b).unwrap());
    let n = sorted.len();
    
    let median = if n % 2 == 1 {
        sorted[n / 2]
    } else {
        (sorted[n / 2 - 1] + sorted[n / 2]) / 2.0
    };
    
    // Compute MAD (Median Absolute Deviation)
    let mut devs: Vec<f64> = sorted.iter()
        .map(|&v| (v - median).abs())
        .collect();
    devs.sort_by(|a, b| a.partial_cmp(b).unwrap());
    
    let mad = if n % 2 == 1 {
        devs[n / 2]
    } else {
        (devs[n / 2 - 1] + devs[n / 2]) / 2.0
    };
    
    // Primary confidence: deviation from median relative to MAD
    let epsilon = 0.001;
    let mad_conf = (value - median).abs() / (mad + epsilon);
    
    // Secondary confidence: relative to range
    let min_val = sorted[0];
    let max_val = sorted[n - 1];
    let range = max_val - min_val;
    
    let range_conf = if range > 1e-9 {
        (value - median).abs() / (range + epsilon)
    } else {
        0.0
    };
    
    // Combine both measures, with MAD being more robust
    mad_conf.max(range_conf * 1.5)
}

Test 21: N-Dimensional Snake Game (C++) Score: 2.00 / 11
Typical Prompt:
You are writing C++ code to play an N-Dimensional Snake Game.

You must write a C++ solver that can handle ANY dimensional complexity from trivial to ludicrous scale:
- **Trivial**: 2D games (eg 8x8), few obstacles, basic pathfinding
- **Medium**: 3D-4D games (eg 6x6x6 to 8x8x8x8), moderate obstacles, intermediate planning
- **Large**: 6D-8D games (eg 4x4x4x4x4x4 to 6x6x6x6x6x6x6x6), many obstacles, complex pathfinding
- **Extreme**: 10D-20D games (eg 3x3x3... to 4x4x4...)

**The Challenge:**
Your C++ snake player will be tested with games ranging from simple 2D boards to massive 20D hypercubes.
The same algorithm must work efficiently across ALL dimensionalities.

**Problem:**
Like classic Nokia snake, but generalized to arbitrary dimensions. The snake occupies a series of
connected integer grid points in N-D space, moves one step per turn along one axis (+1 or -1),
grows when eating food, and dies if it hits an obstacle or itself.

**Input format (stdin, whitespace / newline seperated):**
```
D max_turns (D = number of dimensions, max_turns = turn limit)
bounds (D integers: size of space in each dimension)
snake_length start_pos (length, then D integers for head position)
F (number of food items)
F lines: food positions (D integers each)
O (number of obstacles)
O lines: obstacle positions (D integers each)
```

**Output format (stdout):**
Each turn, output: axis direction
- axis: 0 to D-1 (which dimension to move along)
- direction: -1 or +1 (which way to move)

**Game ends when:**
- Snake eats all food (win)
- Snake hits obstacle or itself (lose)
- Max turns reached

**Environment:**
Platform: Windows 11 (build 10.0.26200)
Architecture: AMD64
CPU: AMD64 Family 23 Model 8 Stepping 2, AuthenticAMD
Core count: 64
Memory: 127.87 GB
SIMD: AVX, AVX2, SSE, SSE2, SSE3, SSE4.1, SSE4.2, SSSE3
SIMD detail: AVX=yes, AVX-512F=no, AVX2=yes, SSE=yes, SSE2=yes, SSE3=yes, SSE4.1=yes, SSE4.2=yes, SSSE3=yes

**C++ Compiler:**
MSVC cl 19.50.35730 | std=c++20 (/std:c++20)

Be sure that any deviation from the C++ standard library is supported by the given compiler,
as referencing the wrong intrinsics or non-standard header like 'bits/stdc++.h' could fail your submission.

Write complete, compilable C++ code with a main() function.

Play the classic Snake game, but in more than two dimensions. The snake moves through an N-dimensional grid, eating food to grow while avoiding its own body and the walls. In higher dimensions the grid is enormous but self-collision becomes far trickier to reason about.

Subpasses increase the number of dimensions, making the state space explode. The AI must write a strategy that plans a safe path to food without boxing itself in.

N-Dimensional Snake - 2D 20x20, 5 food, 10 obstacles

#include <iostream>
#include <vector>
#include <deque>
#include <set>
#include <algorithm>
#include <climits>

int manhattan(const std::vector<int>& a, const std::vector<int>& b) {
    int dist = 0;
    for (size_t i = 0; i < a.size(); ++i) {
        dist += std::abs(a[i] - b[i]);
    }
    return dist;
}

int main() {
    int D, max_turns;
    std::cin >> D >> max_turns;
    std::vector<int> bounds(D);
    for (int i = 0; i < D; ++i) {
        std::cin >> bounds[i];
    }
    int snake_length;
    std::cin >> snake_length;
    std::vector<int> head(D);
    for (int i = 0; i < D; ++i) {
        std::cin >> head[i];
    }
    std::deque<std::vector<int>> snake;
    snake.push_front(head);
    std::set<std::vector<int>> snake_occupied;
    snake_occupied.insert(head);
    std::set<std::vector<int>> foods;
    int F;
    std::cin >> F;
    for (int i = 0; i < F; ++i) {
        std::vector<int> food(D);
        for (int j = 0; j < D; ++j) {
            std::cin >> food[j];
        }
        foods.insert(food);
    }
    std::set<std::vector<int>> obstacles;
    int O;
    std::cin >> O;
    for (int i = 0; i < O; ++i) {
        std::vector<int> obs(D);
        for (int j = 0; j < D; ++j) {
            std::cin >> obs[j];
        }
        obstacles.insert(obs);
    }
    int turn = 0;
    while (turn < max_turns && !foods.empty()) {
        if (foods.empty()) break;
        std::vector<int> target = *foods.begin();
        int min_dist = manhattan(snake.front(), target);
        for (const auto& f : foods) {
            int d = manhattan(snake.front(), f);
            if (d < min_dist) {
                min_dist = d;
                target = f;
            }
        }
        int best_axis = -1;
        int best_dir = 0;
        int best_diff = 0;
        for (int axis = 0; axis < D; ++axis) {
            int diff = target[axis] - snake.front()[axis];
            if (std::abs(diff) > best_diff) {
                best_diff = std::abs(diff);
                best_axis = axis;
                best_dir = (diff > 0 ? 1 : -1);
            }
        }
        std::vector<int> new_head = snake.front();
        if (best_axis != -1) {
            new_head[best_axis] += best_dir;
        }
        bool valid = false;
        if (best_axis != -1) {
            if (new_head[best_axis] >= 0 && new_head[best_axis] < bounds[best_axis] &&
                !obstacles.count(new_head) && !snake_occupied.count(new_head)) {
                valid = true;
            }
        }
        if (!valid) {
            int best_new_dist = INT_MAX;
            int chosen_axis = -1;
            int chosen_dir = 0;
            for (int axis = 0; axis < D; ++axis) {
                for (int dir : {-1, 1}) {
                    std::vector<int> nh = snake.front();
                    nh[axis] += dir;
                    if (nh[axis] < 0 || nh[axis] >= bounds[axis]) continue;
                    if (obstacles.count(nh) || snake_occupied.count(nh)) continue;
                    int new_dist = manhattan(nh, target);
                    if (new_dist < best_new_dist) {
                        best_new_dist = new_dist;
                        chosen_axis = axis;
                        chosen_dir = dir;
                    }
                }
            }
            if (chosen_axis != -1) {
                best_axis = chosen_axis;
                best_dir = chosen_dir;
            } else {
                best_axis = 0;
                best_dir = 1;
                for (int axis = 0; axis < D; ++axis) {
                    for (int dir : {-1, 1}) {
                        std::vector<int> nh = snake.front();
                        nh[axis] += dir;
                        if (nh[axis] >= 0 && nh[axis] < bounds[axis] &&
                            !obstacles.count(nh) && !snake_occupied.count(nh)) {
                            best_axis = axis;
                            best_dir = dir;
                            break;
                        }
                    }
                    if (best_axis != 0 || best_dir != 1) break;
                }
            }
        }
        std::cout << best_axis << " " << best_dir << std::endl;
        std::vector<int> new_pos = snake.front();
        new_pos[best_axis] += best_dir;
        snake.push_front(new_pos);
        snake_occupied.insert(new_pos);
        bool ate = foods.count(new_pos);
        if (ate) {
            foods.erase(new_pos);
        } else {
            if (!snake.empty()) {
                std::vector<int> tail = snake.back();
                snake.pop_back();
                snake_occupied.erase(tail);
            }
        }
        ++turn;
    }
    return 0;
}

Standard Tetris rules apply - variable width board (typically 10-20 columns),
pieces fall from top, clear lines by filling them completely, game over when pieces stack to the top.
The program receives pieces one at a time and must decide optimal placement.

**Input format (stdin, whitespace seperated decimal integers):**
```
width height num_pieces
For each piece:
Line: piece_type (I, O, T, S, Z, J, L)
Program outputs: rotation column
Then receives: result (ok, cleared_N, gameover)
```

**Output format (stdout, 1 line per piece, whitespace seperated decimal integers):**
rotation column
- rotation: 0-3 (number of 90° clockwise rotations)
- column: 0 to width-1 (leftmost column of piece)

**Piece Types:**
- I: 4x1 line piece
- O: 2x2 square piece
- T: T-shaped piece
- S: S-shaped piece (right-leaning)
- Z: Z-shaped piece (left-leaning)
- J: L-shaped piece (left-leaning)
- L: L-shaped piece (right-leaning)

**Requirements:**
1. Program must compile with .NET/csc
2. Read from stdin, write to stdout

Write an AI that plays Tetris. Given the current board state and the next piece, choose where to place it to survive as long as possible and clear as many lines as you can. Good play means keeping the board flat, avoiding buried holes, and setting up multi-line clears.

Subpasses increase the board size and speed, demanding smarter lookahead and evaluation. The AI must balance short-term survival with long-term board health.

using System;
using System.Collections.Generic;

class Program
{
    static void Main()
    {
        string line = Console.ReadLine();
        string[] parts = line.Split(new char[] { ' ', '\t' }, StringSplitOptions.RemoveEmptyEntries);
        int width = int.Parse(parts[0]);
        int height = int.Parse(parts[1]);
        int num_pieces = int.Parse(parts[2]);

        bool[,] board = new bool[height, width];
        int current_piece = 0;

        for (int p = 0; p < num_pieces; p++)
        {
            string piece = Console.ReadLine().Trim();
            if (string.IsNullOrEmpty(piece)) continue;

            current_piece++;

            int best_rot = 0;
            int best_col = 0;
            double best_score = double.MinValue;

            // Adaptive weights based on game complexity (num_pieces as proxy for short vs marathon)
            double line_w = 800;
            double height_w = 1.0;
            double hole_w = 8.0;
            double bump_w = 1.5;

            if (num_pieces < 200)
            {
                // Short practice: aggressive line clearing
                line_w = 1500;
                hole_w = 5.0;
                height_w = 0.8;
            }
            else if (num_pieces > 2000)
            {
                // Marathon: conservative survival focus
                line_w = 300;
                hole_w = 15.0;
                height_w = 1.3;
                bump_w = 2.0;
            }
            else if (num_pieces > 500)
            {
                // Medium-long: balanced but hole-averse
                hole_w = 10.0;
                height_w = 1.1;
            }

            for (int rot = 0; rot < 4; rot++)
            {
                var minos = GetMinos(piece, rot);
                if (minos.Count == 0) continue;

                int min_rx = int.MaxValue;
                int max_rx = int.MinValue;
                foreach (var (_, rx) in minos)
                {
                    if (rx < min_rx) min_rx = rx;
                    if (rx > max_rx) max_rx = rx;
                }
                int piece_width = max_rx - min_rx + 1;

                for (int col = 0; col <= width - piece_width; col++)
                {
                    int top_row = GetDropRow(col, rot, piece, board, height, width);
                    if (!CanPlace(top_row, col, rot, piece, board, height, width)) continue;

                    bool[,] temp = (bool[,])board.Clone();
                    foreach (var (ry, rx) in minos)
                    {
                        int r = top_row + ry;
                        int c = col + rx;
                        if (r < height && c >= 0 && c < width) temp[r, c] = true;
                    }

                    bool[,] new_board = new bool[height, width];
                    int dest = height - 1;
                    int lines = 0;
                    for (int r = height - 1; r >= 0; r--)
                    {
                        if (IsRowFull(temp, r, width))
                        {
                            lines++;
                        }
                        else
                        {
                            for (int c = 0; c < width; c++)
                            {
                                new_board[dest, c] = temp[r, c];
                            }
                            dest--;
                        }
                    }

                    double score = ComputeScore(new_board, height, width, lines, line_w, height_w, hole_w, bump_w);
                    if (score > best_score)
                    {
                        best_score = score;
                        best_rot = rot;
                        best_col = col;
                    }
                }
            }

            if (best_score == double.MinValue)
            {
                best_rot = 0;
                best_col = 0;
            }

            Console.WriteLine(best_rot + " " + best_col);

            string result = Console.ReadLine().Trim();
            if (result == "gameover")
            {
                break;
            }

            // Apply placement to board
            int apply_top_row = GetDropRow(best_col, best_rot, piece, board, height, width);
            var apply_minos = GetMinos(piece, best_rot);
            foreach (var (ry, rx) in apply_minos)
            {
                int r = apply_top_row + ry;
                int c = best_col + rx;
                if (r < height && c >= 0 && c < width) board[r, c] = true;
            }

            // Clear lines on board
            bool[,] cleared_board = new bool[height, width];
            int dest2 = height - 1;
            for (int r = height - 1; r >= 0; r--)
            {
                if (IsRowFull(board, r, width))
                {
                    // cleared
                }
                else
                {
                    for (int c = 0; c < width; c++)
                    {
                        cleared_board[dest2, c] = board[r, c];
                    }
                    dest2--;
                }
            }
            board = cleared_board;
        }
    }

    static List<(int, int)> GetMinos(string type, int rot)
    {
        var minos = new List<(int, int)>();
        rot %= 4;
        if (type == "I")
        {
            if (rot % 2 == 0)
            {
                minos.Add((0, 0)); minos.Add((0, 1)); minos.Add((0, 2)); minos.Add((0, 3));
            }
            else
            {
                minos.Add((0, 0)); minos.Add((1, 0)); minos.Add((2, 0)); minos.Add((3, 0));
            }
        }
        else if (type == "O")
        {
            minos.Add((0, 0)); minos.Add((0, 1)); minos.Add((1, 0)); minos.Add((1, 1));
        }
        else if (type == "T")
        {
            if (rot == 0)
            {
                minos.Add((0, 1)); minos.Add((1, 0)); minos.Add((1, 1)); minos.Add((1, 2));
            }
            else if (rot == 1)
            {
                minos.Add((0, 0)); minos.Add((1, 0)); minos.Add((1, 1)); minos.Add((2, 0));
            }
            else if (rot == 2)
            {
                minos.Add((0, 0)); minos.Add((0, 1)); minos.Add((0, 2)); minos.Add((1, 1));
            }
            else if (rot == 3)
            {
                minos.Add((0, 1)); minos.Add((1, 0)); minos.Add((1, 1)); minos.Add((2, 1));
            }
        }
        else if (type == "S")
        {
            if (rot % 2 == 0)
            {
                minos.Add((0, 1)); minos.Add((0, 2)); minos.Add((1, 0)); minos.Add((1, 1));
            }
            else
            {
                minos.Add((0, 0)); minos.Add((1, 0)); minos.Add((1, 1)); minos.Add((2, 1));
            }
        }
        else if (type == "Z")
        {
            if (rot % 2 == 0)
            {
                minos.Add((0, 0)); minos.Add((0, 1)); minos.Add((1, 1)); minos.Add((1, 2));
            }
            else
            {
                minos.Add((0, 1)); minos.Add((1, 0)); minos.Add((1, 1)); minos.Add((2, 0));
            }
        }
        else if (type == "J")
        {
            if (rot == 0)
            {
                minos.Add((0, 1)); minos.Add((1, 1)); minos.Add((2, 0)); minos.Add((2, 1));
            }
            else if (rot == 1)
            {
                minos.Add((0, 0)); minos.Add((1, 0)); minos.Add((1, 1)); minos.Add((1, 2));
            }
            else if (rot == 2)
            {
                minos.Add((0, 0)); minos.Add((0, 1)); minos.Add((1, 0)); minos.Add((2, 0));
            }
            else if (rot == 3)
            {
                minos.Add((0, 0)); minos.Add((0, 1)); minos.Add((0, 2)); minos.Add((1, 0));
            }
        }
        else if (type == "L")
        {
            if (rot == 0)
            {
                minos.Add((0, 0)); minos.Add((1, 0)); minos.Add((2, 0)); minos.Add((2, 1));
            }
            else if (rot == 1)
            {
                minos.Add((0, 0)); minos.Add((0, 1)); minos.Add((0, 2)); minos.Add((1, 0));
            }
            else if (rot == 2)
            {
                minos.Add((0, 0)); minos.Add((0, 1)); minos.Add((1, 1)); minos.Add((2, 1));
            }
            else if (rot == 3)
            {
                minos.Add((0, 2)); minos.Add((1, 0)); minos.Add((1, 1)); minos.Add((1, 2));
            }
        }
        return minos;
    }

    static bool CanPlace(int top_row, int left_col, int rot, string type, bool[,] board, int height, int width)
    {
        var minos = GetMinos(type, rot);
        foreach (var (ry, rx) in minos)
        {
            int r = top_row + ry;
            int c = left_col + rx;
            if (r >= height || c < 0 || c >= width || board[r, c]) return false;
        }
        return true;
    }

    static int GetDropRow(int left_col, int rot, string type, bool[,] board, int height, int width)
    {
        int top_row = 0;
        while (CanPlace(top_row + 1, left_col, rot, type, board, height, width))
        {
            top_row++;
        }
        return top_row;
    }

    static bool IsRowFull(bool[,] b, int r, int w)
    {
        for (int c = 0; c < w; c++)
            if (!b[r, c]) return false;
        return true;
    }

    static double ComputeScore(bool[,] b, int h, int w, int lines_cleared, double line_w, double height_w, double hole_w, double bump_w)
    {
        int agg_height = 0;
        int holes = 0;
        int bump = 0;
        int[] heights = new int[w];

        for (int c = 0; c < w; c++)
        {
            heights[c] = 0;
            for (int r = 0; r < h; r++)
            {
                if (b[r, c])
                {
                    heights[c] = h - r;
                    break;
                }
            }
            agg_height += heights[c];
        }

        for (int c = 0; c < w; c++)
        {
            bool has_above = false;
            for (int r = 0; r < h; r++)
            {
                if (b[r, c]) has_above = true;
                else if (has_above) holes++;
            }
        }

        for (int c = 0; c < w - 1; c++)
        {
            bump += Math.Abs(heights[c] - heights[c + 1]);
        }

        double score = lines_cleared * line_w - agg_height * height_w - holes * hole_w - bump * bump_w;
        return score;
    }
}

using System;
using System.Collections.Generic;

class Program
{
    static void Main()
    {
        string line = Console.ReadLine();
        string[] parts = line.Split(new char[] { ' ', '\t' }, StringSplitOptions.RemoveEmptyEntries);
        int width = int.Parse(parts[0]);
        int height = int.Parse(parts[1]);
        int num_pieces = int.Parse(parts[2]);

        bool[,] board = new bool[height, width];
        int current_piece = 0;

        for (int p = 0; p < num_pieces; p++)
        {
            string piece = Console.ReadLine().Trim();
            if (string.IsNullOrEmpty(piece)) continue;

            current_piece++;

            int best_rot = 0;
            int best_col = 0;
            double best_score = double.MinValue;

            // Adaptive weights based on game complexity (num_pieces as proxy for short vs marathon)
            double line_w = 800;
            double height_w = 1.0;
            double hole_w = 8.0;
            double bump_w = 1.5;

            if (num_pieces < 200)
            {
                // Short practice: aggressive line clearing
                line_w = 1500;
                hole_w = 5.0;
                height_w = 0.8;
            }
            else if (num_pieces > 2000)
            {
                // Marathon: conservative survival focus
                line_w = 300;
                hole_w = 15.0;
                height_w = 1.3;
                bump_w = 2.0;
            }
            else if (num_pieces > 500)
            {
                // Medium-long: balanced but hole-averse
                hole_w = 10.0;
                height_w = 1.1;
            }

            for (int rot = 0; rot < 4; rot++)
            {
                var minos = GetMinos(piece, rot);
                if (minos.Count == 0) continue;

                int min_rx = int.MaxValue;
                int max_rx = int.MinValue;
                foreach (var (_, rx) in minos)
                {
                    if (rx < min_rx) min_rx = rx;
                    if (rx > max_rx) max_rx = rx;
                }
                int piece_width = max_rx - min_rx + 1;

                for (int col = 0; col <= width - piece_width; col++)
                {
                    int top_row = GetDropRow(col, rot, piece, board, height, width);
                    if (!CanPlace(top_row, col, rot, piece, board, height, width)) continue;

                    bool[,] temp = (bool[,])board.Clone();
                    foreach (var (ry, rx) in minos)
                    {
                        int r = top_row + ry;
                        int c = col + rx;
                        if (r < height && c >= 0 && c < width) temp[r, c] = true;
                    }

                    bool[,] new_board = new bool[height, width];
                    int dest = height - 1;
                    int lines = 0;
                    for (int r = height - 1; r >= 0; r--)
                    {
                        if (IsRowFull(temp, r, width))
                        {
                            lines++;
                        }
                        else
                        {
                            for (int c = 0; c < width; c++)
                            {
                                new_board[dest, c] = temp[r, c];
                            }
                            dest--;
                        }
                    }

                    double score = ComputeScore(new_board, height, width, lines, line_w, height_w, hole_w, bump_w);
                    if (score > best_score)
                    {
                        best_score = score;
                        best_rot = rot;
                        best_col = col;
                    }
                }
            }

            if (best_score == double.MinValue)
            {
                best_rot = 0;
                best_col = 0;
            }

            Console.WriteLine(best_rot + " " + best_col);

            string result = Console.ReadLine().Trim();
            if (result == "gameover")
            {
                break;
            }

            // Apply placement to board
            int apply_top_row = GetDropRow(best_col, best_rot, piece, board, height, width);
            var apply_minos = GetMinos(piece, best_rot);
            foreach (var (ry, rx) in apply_minos)
            {
                int r = apply_top_row + ry;
                int c = best_col + rx;
                if (r < height && c >= 0 && c < width) board[r, c] = true;
            }

            // Clear lines on board
            bool[,] cleared_board = new bool[height, width];
            int dest2 = height - 1;
            for (int r = height - 1; r >= 0; r--)
            {
                if (IsRowFull(board, r, width))
                {
                    // cleared
                }
                else
                {
                    for (int c = 0; c < width; c++)
                    {
                        cleared_board[dest2, c] = board[r, c];
                    }
                    dest2--;
                }
            }
            board = cleared_board;
        }
    }

    static List<(int, int)> GetMinos(string type, int rot)
    {
        var minos = new List<(int, int)>();
        rot %= 4;
        if (type == "I")
        {
            if (rot % 2 == 0)
            {
                minos.Add((0, 0)); minos.Add((0, 1)); minos.Add((0, 2)); minos.Add((0, 3));
            }
            else
            {
                minos.Add((0, 0)); minos.Add((1, 0)); minos.Add((2, 0)); minos.Add((3, 0));
            }
        }
        else if (type == "O")
        {
            minos.Add((0, 0)); minos.Add((0, 1)); minos.Add((1, 0)); minos.Add((1, 1));
        }
        else if (type == "T")
        {
            if (rot == 0)
            {
                minos.Add((0, 1)); minos.Add((1, 0)); minos.Add((1, 1)); minos.Add((1, 2));
            }
            else if (rot == 1)
            {
                minos.Add((0, 0)); minos.Add((1, 0)); minos.Add((1, 1)); minos.Add((2, 0));
            }
            else if (rot == 2)
            {
                minos.Add((0, 0)); minos.Add((0, 1)); minos.Add((0, 2)); minos.Add((1, 1));
            }
            else if (rot == 3)
            {
                minos.Add((0, 1)); minos.Add((1, 0)); minos.Add((1, 1)); minos.Add((2, 1));
            }
        }
        else if (type == "S")
        {
            if (rot % 2 == 0)
            {
                minos.Add((0, 1)); minos.Add((0, 2)); minos.Add((1, 0)); minos.Add((1, 1));
            }
            else
            {
                minos.Add((0, 0)); minos.Add((1, 0)); minos.Add((1, 1)); minos.Add((2, 1));
            }
        }
        else if (type == "Z")
        {
            if (rot % 2 == 0)
            {
                minos.Add((0, 0)); minos.Add((0, 1)); minos.Add((1, 1)); minos.Add((1, 2));
            }
            else
            {
                minos.Add((0, 1)); minos.Add((1, 0)); minos.Add((1, 1)); minos.Add((2, 0));
            }
        }
        else if (type == "J")
        {
            if (rot == 0)
            {
                minos.Add((0, 1)); minos.Add((1, 1)); minos.Add((2, 0)); minos.Add((2, 1));
            }
            else if (rot == 1)
            {
                minos.Add((0, 0)); minos.Add((1, 0)); minos.Add((1, 1)); minos.Add((1, 2));
            }
            else if (rot == 2)
            {
                minos.Add((0, 0)); minos.Add((0, 1)); minos.Add((1, 0)); minos.Add((2, 0));
            }
            else if (rot == 3)
            {
                minos.Add((0, 0)); minos.Add((0, 1)); minos.Add((0, 2)); minos.Add((1, 0));
            }
        }
        else if (type == "L")
        {
            if (rot == 0)
            {
                minos.Add((0, 0)); minos.Add((1, 0)); minos.Add((2, 0)); minos.Add((2, 1));
            }
            else if (rot == 1)
            {
                minos.Add((0, 0)); minos.Add((0, 1)); minos.Add((0, 2)); minos.Add((1, 0));
            }
            else if (rot == 2)
            {
                minos.Add((0, 0)); minos.Add((0, 1)); minos.Add((1, 1)); minos.Add((2, 1));
            }
            else if (rot == 3)
            {
                minos.Add((0, 2)); minos.Add((1, 0)); minos.Add((1, 1)); minos.Add((1, 2));
            }
        }
        return minos;
    }

    static bool CanPlace(int top_row, int left_col, int rot, string type, bool[,] board, int height, int width)
    {
        var minos = GetMinos(type, rot);
        foreach (var (ry, rx) in minos)

    {

Typical Prompt:
You are writing Rust code to play Lunar Lander in real-time.

Your Rust lunar lander controller will be tested with scenarios ranging from simple
training environments to very complex landing sites.

Control a lunar lander to safely land on a target pad.
The program receives a 2D voxel map and continuous state updates, and must output thrust/turn
commands to land safely on the target.

Data is streamed to stdin in real time, and you must write to stdout in real time. If your code
doesn't read from stdin fast enough and the io buffer fills up, the ship will likely crash.

Be very careful if writing single threaded / blocking code, this has many failure modes that
async code doesn't have. Multithreaded / asyncio code is HIGHLY recommended.

**Physics:**
- Gravity pulls lander down constantly
- Thrust applies force in lander's facing direction
- Fuel is limited
- Must land softly on target (low velocity)

**Input format (stdin, whitespace seperated decimal numbers):**
Initial map:
```
width height gravity max_thrust fuel
start_x start_y target_x target_y
map rows (. = empty, # = obstacle, S = start, T = target, L = landing zone)
```

Then you recieve continuous state updates (every 0.1 seconds):
```
x y vx vy angle angular_vel fuel_remaining
```
x and y are in meters, from the worlds top left, and y increases downward.
vx and vy are in m/s.
angle is in radians, 0 is facing up.
angular_vel is in radians per second. + is clockwise, - is counterclockwise.
fuel_remaining is seconds at max_thrust.

**Output format (stdout):**
Your code needs to output the following instructions at a frequency of at least 20hz:
```
thrust turn
```
- thrust: 0.0 to 1.0 (fraction of max thrust)
- turn: -1.0 to 1.0 (turning rate, negative = left, positive = right)

To be crystal clear: that's two decimal numbers seperated by a space, followed by a newline.

If your code stalls / freezes for 100ms or more (so it misses 2 consecutive updates), the engine
will automatically cut power. A long freeze and eventually the lander will crash.

Map size can vary from 100x50 to multi-gb maps, so be efficient with memory and processing.

Thrust and gravity are in m/s/s. 100% engine burn burns 1 unit of fuel per second.

Lander size is approximatly 1x1m, and the 2D map grid size is 1m x 1m.

Turn is in radians per second. The lander can not rotate fully around and will clamp rotation to
facing down if attempted.

Y increases downward. Positive vy means moving downward. Gravity is +g.

**Success Conditions:**
- Land on target with |velocity| < 2m/s
- Stay within landing zone boundaries
- Complete landing within time limit

**Failure Conditions:**
- Crash into obstacle or ground too hard
- Run out of fuel
- Exceed time limit

Architecture: AMD64
CPU: AMD64 Family 23 Model 8 Stepping 2, AuthenticAMD

rustc 1.92.0 (ded5c06cf 2025-12-08) | edition=2024 | host: x86_64-pc-windows-msvc

Test 24: 3D Lunar Lander Game (C++) Score: 0.00 / 10
Typical Prompt:
You are writing C++ code to play a 3D Lunar Lander game in real-time.

Your C++ controller will be tested with scenarios ranging from tiny (100m) to huge (100km).
The same code must work for all scales.

Control a lunar lander in full 3D space to safely land on a target pad.
The program receives a terrain file path and continuous state updates via stdin, and must
output thrust/rotation commands to stdout in real-time.

Data is streamed to stdin in real time, and you must write to stdout in real time.
If your code doesn't read from stdin fast enough and the IO buffer fills up, the ship
will likely crash.

Be very careful if writing single threaded / blocking code, this has many failure modes
that async code doesn't have. Multithreaded code is HIGHLY recommended.

**Coordinate System:**
- X: horizontal (East), Y: horizontal (North), Z: UP.
- Gravity acts in the -Z direction.
- All positions are in meters. Velocities in m/s. Angles in radians.

**Physics:**
- Gravity = 1.62 m/s² (lunar) in -Z direction.
- Thrust is along the lander's local "up" axis. When pitch=0 and yaw=0, thrust is
straight up (+Z). Tilting via pitch/yaw redirects thrust.
- Pitch: tilts the lander. +pitch tilts forward, redirecting thrust partially into -X.
Pitch is clamped to [-pi/2, pi/2].
- Yaw: rotates heading around Z.
- Roll: rolls around the thrust axis (cosmetic only, does not affect thrust direction).
- Rotation dynamics: commands apply angular acceleration (2 rad/s² per unit).
Angular rates are damped by 0.95 per tick.
- Fuel: 100% thrust burns 1 unit of fuel per second.

**Input format (stdin):**
Initial header (whitespace separated decimal numbers, except terrain path):
```
width depth height gravity max_thrust fuel
start_x start_y start_z target_x target_y target_z
terrain_file_path
STATE
```

The terrain_file_path is on its own line (the path may contain spaces).
Read the entire line with getline() or equivalent.

**Terrain file format (binary):**
The terrain file defines the 3D world as a binary file. It is a sequence of
uint16_t triplets (little-endian), one per (x, y) cell, stored in row-major order:

```cpp
for (int x = 0; x < width; x++) {
for (int y = 0; y < depth; y++) {
uint16_t a = read_uint16_le(); // ground rock top
uint16_t b = read_uint16_le(); // floating rock bottom
uint16_t c = read_uint16_le(); // floating rock top
}
}
```

For each column (x, y), the vertical structure is:
- z < a: SOLID ROCK (ground)
- a <= z < b: OPEN AIR
- b <= z < c: SOLID ROCK (floating terrain feature, overhang, arch, etc.)
- c <= z: OPEN AIR

If b == c, there is no floating rock in that column (just ground + open sky).
The file size is exactly width * depth * 6 bytes.

You have a startup grace period to parse this file before state updates begin.
The grace period is 5 seconds plus 10 seconds per gigabyte of terrain file.
For a 100x100 map this is ~5s. For a 100000x10000 map (~6GB) this is ~65s.
You may continue parsing in a background thread after the simulation begins,
but you MUST be reading stdin and writing stdout by then to avoid a crash.

Then continuous state updates (every 0.1 seconds, whitespace separated):
```
x y z vx vy vz pitch yaw roll pitch_rate yaw_rate roll_rate fuel_remaining
```

**Output format (stdout):**
Your code needs to output the following at a frequency of at least 10hz:
```
thrust pitch_cmd yaw_cmd roll_cmd
```
- thrust: 0.0 to 1.0 (fraction of max_thrust)
- pitch_cmd: -1.0 to 1.0 (pitch angular acceleration command)
- yaw_cmd: -1.0 to 1.0 (yaw angular acceleration command)
- roll_cmd: -1.0 to 1.0 (roll angular acceleration command)

To be crystal clear: four decimal numbers separated by spaces, followed by a newline.

If your code stalls / freezes for 100ms or more (misses 2 consecutive updates), the
engine will cut thrust automatically. A long freeze and eventually the lander will crash.

**Landing:**
- The target is at (target_x, target_y, target_z) which is just above the terrain.
- You must land within a small radius of the target with total speed < 3 m/s.

#include <iostream>
#include <vector>
#include <thread>
#include <atomic>
#include <fstream>
#include <string>
#include <cmath>
#include <algorithm>
#include <limits>
#include <ios>

int main() {
    std::ios::sync_with_stdio(false);
    std::cin.tie(nullptr);
    std::cout.tie(nullptr);

    double width, depth, height, grav, max_thrust, fuel;
    double sx, sy, sz, tx, ty, tz;
    std::cin >> width >> depth >> height >> grav >> max_thrust >> fuel;
    std::cin >> sx >> sy >> sz >> tx >> ty >> tz;

    std::string terrain_path;
    std::cin.ignore(std::numeric_limits<std::streamsize>::max(), '\n');
    std::getline(std::cin, terrain_path);

    std::atomic<bool> terrain_ready{false};
    std::vector<uint16_t> terrain_data;
    std::thread terrain_parser([&]() {
        std::ifstream tfile(terrain_path, std::ios::binary);
        if (tfile) {
            size_t expected = static_cast<size_t>(width) * static_cast<size_t>(depth) * 6ULL;
            tfile.seekg(0, std::ios::end);
            size_t fsize = tfile.tellg();
            if (fsize == expected) {
                tfile.seekg(0, std::ios::beg);
                terrain_data.resize(static_cast<size_t>(width) * static_cast<size_t>(depth) * 3ULL);
                tfile.read(reinterpret_cast<char*>(terrain_data.data()), fsize);
            }
        }
        terrain_ready = true;
    });

    const double Kp = 0.05;
    const double Kd = 0.8;
    const double att_Kp = 4.0;
    const double att_Kd = 1.5;
    const double PI = 3.14159265358979323846;

    while (true) {
        double x, y, z, vx, vy, vz, pitch, yaw, roll, prate, yrate, rrate, fuel_rem;
        if (!(std::cin >> x >> y >> z >> vx >> vy >> vz >> pitch >> yaw >> roll >> prate >> yrate >> rrate >> fuel_rem)) {
            break;
        }

        double ex = tx - x;
        double ey = ty - y;
        double ez = tz - z;

        double ax = Kp * ex - Kd * vx;
        double ay = Kp * ey - Kd * vy;
        double az = Kp * ez - Kd * vz + grav;

        double force_mag = std::sqrt(ax * ax + ay * ay + az * az);
        double tdx = (force_mag > 1e-9) ? (ax / force_mag) : 0.0;
        double tdy = (force_mag > 1e-9) ? (ay / force_mag) : 0.0;
        double tdz = (force_mag > 1e-9) ? (az / force_mag) : 1.0;

        double hmag = std::sqrt(tdx * tdx + tdy * tdy);
        double desired_pitch = 0.0;
        double desired_yaw = yaw;
        double desired_roll = 0.0;

        if (hmag > 1e-6) {
            double vx_dir = tdx / hmag;
            double vy_dir = tdy / hmag;
            desired_yaw = std::atan2(-vy_dir, -vx_dir);
            desired_pitch = std::asin(hmag);
        }

        double pitch_err = desired_pitch - pitch;
        double pitch_cmd = att_Kp * pitch_err - att_Kd * prate;
        pitch_cmd = std::max(-1.0, std::min(1.0, pitch_cmd));

        double yaw_err = desired_yaw - yaw;
        while (yaw_err > PI) yaw_err -= 2.0 * PI;
        while (yaw_err < -PI) yaw_err += 2.0 * PI;
        double yaw_cmd = att_Kp * yaw_err - att_Kd * yrate;
        yaw_cmd = std::max(-1.0, std::min(1.0, yaw_cmd));

        double roll_err = desired_roll - roll;
        double roll_cmd = att_Kp * roll_err - att_Kd * rrate;
        roll_cmd = std::max(-1.0, std::min(1.0, roll_cmd));

        double thrust = (max_thrust > 1e-9) ? (force_mag / max_thrust) : 0.0;
        thrust = std::max(0.0, std::min(1.0, thrust));

        double hdist = std::sqrt(ex * ex + ey * ey);
        double speed = std::sqrt(vx * vx + vy * vy + vz * vz);
        if (hdist < 8.0 && std::abs(ez) < 10.0 && speed < 4.0) {
            thrust = 0.25;
        }

        std::cout << thrust << " " << pitch_cmd << " " << yaw_cmd << " " << roll_cmd << "\n";
    }

    terrain_parser.join();
    return 0;
}

Typical Prompt:
You are writing Rust code to cluster 3D points into exactly N clusters.

You must write a Rust solver that can handle ANY clustering scenario from trivial to ludicrous scale:
- **Trivial**: Small datasets (1M points, 10 clusters), basic k-means, memory-friendly
- **Medium**: Moderate datasets (10M points, 100 clusters), optimized k-means, streaming
- **Large**: Large datasets (100M points, 1000 clusters), mini-batch k-means, memory constraints
- **Extreme**: Massive datasets (1B-10B points, 10000 clusters), streaming algorithms, very tight memory

**The Challenge:**
Your Rust clustering algorithm will be tested with datasets ranging from millions to billions of 3D points. The same algorithm must work efficiently across ALL scales while respecting memory constraints.

**Problem:**
Given millions to billions of 3D points, partition them into exactly N clusters minimizing within-cluster variance (k-means objective). Points are provided as binary float32 triples for efficiency.

**Input format (stdin):**
```
num_points num_clusters
[x y z] (as binary float32 triples, num_points total)
```

**Output format (stdout):**
```
[cluster_index] (as binary uint32, one per point)
```

**Critical Requirements:**
1. **Scalability**: Your algorithm must adapt based on point count and cluster count
2. **Performance**: Must complete within 5 minutes even for massive datasets
3. **Memory**: Must handle streaming input for datasets that don't fit in memory
4. **Quality**: Minimize within-cluster variance while producing exactly N clusters

**Algorithm Strategy Recommendations:**
- **Small datasets (≤10M points)**: Can use standard k-means with full data in memory
- **Medium datasets (10M-100M points)**: Mini-batch k-means, streaming updates
- **Large datasets (100M-1B points)**: Streaming k-means with limited memory buffers
- **Very Large datasets (>1B points)**: Very fast streaming, approximate clustering

**Key Techniques:**
- **Streaming algorithms**: Process points in batches without storing all data
- **Mini-batch k-means**: Update centroids incrementally
- **Memory management**: Use fixed-size buffers for large datasets
- **Binary I/O**: Efficient reading/writing of binary data
- **Convergence detection**: Monitor when clustering stabilizes

**Implementation Hints:**
- Detect dataset size and choose appropriate clustering algorithm
- Use efficient binary I/O (std::io::BufReader/BufWriter)
- Implement streaming updates for large datasets
- For very large datasets, use approximation algorithms
- Handle edge cases: empty clusters, convergence issues
- Use fast random access for centroid updates

**Binary Format Details:**
- Input: Points as little-endian f32 triples (12 bytes per point)
- Output: Cluster indices as little-endian u32 (4 bytes per point)
- Total input size: num_points × 12 bytes
- Total output size: num_points × 4 bytes

**Memory Constraints:**
- Small datasets: Can load all points into memory
- Medium datasets: Use streaming with moderate buffers
- Large datasets: Streaming with minimal memory footprint
- Very Large datasets: Extremely memory-efficient streaming

**Requirements:**
1. Program must compile with rustc (edition 2021)
2. Read binary input from stdin, write binary output to stdout
3. Handle variable point counts and cluster numbers
4. Complete within 5 minutes
5. Must handle varying dataset sizes efficiently
6. Produce exactly N clusters

Include adaptive logic that chooses different strategies based on clustering complexity.

use std::io::{self, Read, Write, BufReader, BufWriter};

fn main() {
    let mut line = String::new();
    io::stdin().read_line(&mut line).expect("read header");
    let mut parts = line.trim().split_whitespace();
    let num_points: u64 = parts.next().unwrap().parse().expect("num_points");
    let num_clusters: usize = parts.next().unwrap().parse().expect("num_clusters");

    if num_clusters == 0 || num_points == 0 {
        return;
    }

    let mut reader = BufReader::new(io::stdin());
    let mut writer = BufWriter::new(io::stdout());

    // Adaptive strategy selection
    let is_very_large = num_points > 500_000_000 || num_clusters > 5000;
    let is_large = num_points > 50_000_000 || num_clusters > 500;

        }

        let assignments = full_kmeans(&points, num_clusters, is_medium);
        for a in assignments {

        }
    } else {
        // Streaming online k-means (handles up to billions of points)

        let mut initialized = false;

// Full k-means implementation for small datasets
fn full_kmeans(points: &[[f32; 3]], k: usize, is_medium: bool) -> Vec<u32> {
    if points.is_empty() || k == 0 {
        return vec![];
    }

    let max_iter = if is_medium { 8 } else { 20 };
    let mut centroids: Vec<[f32; 3]> = points[..k.min(points.len())].to_vec();
    let mut assignments = vec![0u32; points.len()];

    for _ in 0..max_iter {
        let mut new_centroids = vec![[0.0f32; 3]; k];
        let mut counts = vec![0u64; k];
        let mut changed = false;

        for (i, point) in points.iter().enumerate() {
            let mut best = 0;
            let mut min_dist = f32::MAX;
            for (j, c) in centroids.iter().enumerate() {
                let dx = point[0] - c[0];
                let dy = point[1] - c[1];
                let dz = point[2] - c[2];
                let dist = dx * dx + dy * dy + dz * dz;
                if dist < min_dist {
                    min_dist = dist;
                    best = j;
                }
            }
            assignments[i] = best as u32;

            for d in 0..3 {
                new_centroids[best][d] += point[d];
            }
            counts[best] += 1;
        }

        // Update centroids and check convergence
        for i in 0..k {
            if counts[i] > 0 {
                let inv = 1.0 / counts[i] as f32;
                for d in 0..3 {
                    let new_val = new_centroids[i][d] * inv;
                    if (new_val - centroids[i][d]).abs() > 1e-3 {
                        changed = true;
                    }
                    centroids[i][d] = new_val;
                }
            }
        }

        if !changed {
            break;
        }
    }

    assignments
}

use std::io::{self, Read, Write, BufReader, BufWriter};

fn main() {
    let mut line = String::new();
    io::stdin().read_line(&mut line).expect("read header");
    let mut parts = line.trim().split_whitespace();
    let num_points: u64 = parts.next().unwrap().parse().expect("num_points");
    let num_clusters: usize = parts.next().unwrap().parse().expect("num_clusters");

    if num_clusters == 0 || num_points == 0 {
        return;
    }

    let mut reader = BufReader::new(io::stdin());
    let mut writer = BufWriter::new(io::stdout());

    // Adaptive strategy selection
    let is_very_large = num_points > 500_000_000 || num_clusters > 5000;
    let is_large = num_points > 50_000_000 || num_clusters > 500;
    let is_medium = num_points > 5_000_000 || num_clusters > 100;

    // Use streaming online k-means for all scales (memory O(num_clusters))
    // Full in-memory k-means only for tiny datasets to guarantee quality
    let use_full_kmeans = num_points <= 2_000_000 && num_clusters <= 200;

    if use_full_kmeans {
        // Load all points (memory-friendly for small cases)
        let mut points: Vec<[f32; 3]> = Vec::with_capacity(num_points as usize);
        let mut buf = [0u8; 12];
        for _ in 0..num_points {
            if reader.read_exact(&mut buf).is_err() {
                break;
            }
            let x = f32::from_le_bytes([buf[0], buf[1], buf[2], buf[3]]);
            let y = f32::from_le_bytes([buf[4], buf[5], buf[6], buf[7]]);
            let z = f32::from_le_bytes([buf[8], buf[9], buf[10], buf[11]]);
            points.push([x, y, z]);
        }

        // Full k-means with limited iterations for performance
        let assignments = full_kmeans(&points, num_clusters, is_medium);
        for a in assignments {
            writer.write_all(&a.to_le_bytes()).expect("write");
        }
    } else {
        // Streaming online k-means (handles up to billions of points)
        let mut centroids: Vec<[f32; 3]> = vec![[0.0; 3]; num_clusters];
        let mut counts: Vec<u64> = vec![0; num_clusters];
        let mut initialized = false;
        let mut point_idx: u64 = 0;

        let mut buf = [0u8; 12];
        while point_idx < num_points {
            if reader.read_exact(&mut buf).is_err() {
                break;
            }

            let x = f32::from_le_bytes([buf[0], buf[1], buf[2], buf[3]]);
            let y = f32::from_le_bytes([buf[4], buf[5], buf[6], buf[7]]);
            let z = f32::from_le_bytes([buf[8], buf[9], buf[10], buf[11]]);
            let point = [x, y, z];

            // Initialize centroids with first points
            if !initialized && point_idx < num_clusters as u64 {
                centroids[point_idx as usize] = point;
                counts[point_idx as usize] = 1;
                let cluster = point_idx as u32;
                writer.write_all(&cluster.to_le_bytes()).expect("write");
                point_idx += 1;
                continue;
            }

            if !initialized {
                initialized = true;
            }

            // Find nearest centroid
            let mut best = 0usize;
            let mut min_dist = f32::MAX;
            for (i, c) in centroids.iter().enumerate() {
                let dx = point[0] - c[0];
                let dy = point[1] - c[1];
                let dz = point[2] - c[2];
                let dist = dx * dx + dy * dy + dz * dz;
                if dist < min_dist {
                    min_dist = dist;
                    best = i;
                }
            }

            // Adaptive learning rate based on scale
            let count = counts[best];
            let lr = if is_very_large {
                1.0 / ((count as f32 + 1.0).sqrt() + 1.0)
            } else if is_large {
                1.0 / (count as f32 + 10.0)
            } else if is_medium {
                1.0 / (count as f32 + 5.0)
            } else {
                1.0 / (count as f32 + 1.0)
            };

            // Update centroid
            if count == 0 {
                centroids[best] = point;
            } else {
                for j in 0..3 {
                    centroids[best][j] = centroids[best][j] * (1.0 - lr) + point[j] * lr;
                }
            }
            counts[best] += 1;

            // Output assignment
            writer.write_all(&(best as u32).to_le_bytes()).expect("write");
            point_idx += 1;
        }
    }

    writer.flush().expect("flush");
}

// Full k-means implementation for small datasets
fn full_kmeans(points: &[[f32; 3]], k: usize, is_medium: bool) -> Vec<u32> {
    if points.is_empty() || k == 0 {
        return vec![];
    }

    let max_iter = if is_medium { 8 } else { 20 };
    let mut centroids: Vec<[f32; 3]> = points[..k.min(points.len())].to_vec();
    let mut assignments = vec![0u32; points.len()];

    for _ in 0..max_iter {
        let mut new_centroids = vec![[0.0f32; 3]; k];
        let mut counts = vec![0u64; k];
        let mut changed = false;

        for (i, point) in points.iter().enumerate() {
            let mut best = 0;
            let mut min_dist = f32::MAX;
            for (j, c) in centroids.iter().enumerate() {
                let dx = point[0] - c[0];
                let dy = point[1] - c[1];
                let dz = point[2] - c[2];
                let dist = dx * dx + dy * dy + dz * dz;
                if dist < min_dist {
                    min_dist = dist;
                    best = j;
                }
            }
            assignments[i] = best as u32;

            for d in 0..3 {
                new_centroids[best][d] += point[d];
            }
            counts[best] += 1;
        }

        // Update centroids and check convergence
        for i in 0..k {
            if counts[i] > 0 {
                let inv = 1.0 / counts[i] as f32;
                for d in 0..3 {
                    let new_val = new_centroids[i][d] * inv;
                    if (new_val - centroids[i][d]).abs() > 1e-3 {
                        changed = true;
                    }
                    centroids[i][d] = new_val;
                }
            }
        }

        if !changed {
            break;
        }
    }

    assignments
}

#include <iostream>
#include <vector>
#include <algorithm>
#include <numeric>
#include <cstdint>

int main() {
    std::ios::sync_with_stdio(false);
    std::cin.tie(nullptr);
    
    int n, m, k;
    std::cin >> n >> m >> k;
    
    std::vector<std::vector<int>> adj(n);
    for (int i = 0; i < m; ++i) {
        int u, v;
        std::cin >> u >> v;
        adj[u].push_back(v);
        adj[v].push_back(u);
    }
    
    // Remove duplicates
    for (auto& lst : adj) {
        std::sort(lst.begin(), lst.end());
        auto it = std::unique(lst.begin(), lst.end());
        lst.resize(it - lst.begin());
    }
    
    std::vector<int> degree(n);
    for (int i = 0; i < n; ++i) {
        degree[i] = adj[i].size();
    }
    
    std::vector<int> color(n, -1);
    
    // Greedy coloring with degree ordering
    std::vector<int> order(n);
    std::iota(order.begin(), order.end(), 0);
    std::sort(order.begin(), order.end(), [&](int x, int y) {
        return degree[x] > degree[y] || (degree[x] == degree[y] && x < y);
    });
    
    bool success = true;
    for (int v : order) {
        uint64_t forbidden = 0;
        for (int nei : adj[v]) {
            if (color[nei] != -1) {
                if (color[nei] < 64) {
                    forbidden |= (1ULL << color[nei]);
                }
            }
        }
        bool assigned = false;
        for (int c = 0; c < k; ++c) {
            if (c >= 64 || (forbidden & (1ULL << c)) == 0) {
                color[v] = c;
                assigned = true;
                break;
            }
        }
        if (!assigned) {
            success = false;
            break;
        }
    }
    
    if (!success && n <= 100) {
        // Fallback to backtracking for small graphs
        std::fill(color.begin(), color.end(), -1);
        
        std::vector<int> bt_order(n);
        std::iota(bt_order.begin(), bt_order.end(), 0);
        std::sort(bt_order.begin(), bt_order.end(), [&](int x, int y) {
            return degree[x] > degree[y] || (degree[x] == degree[y] && x < y);
        });
        
        auto solve = [&](auto&& self, int pos) -> bool {
            if (pos == n) return true;
            int v = bt_order[pos];
            uint64_t forbidden = 0;
            for (int nei : adj[v]) {
                if (color[nei] != -1 && color[nei] < 64) {
                    forbidden |= (1ULL << color[nei]);
                }
            }
            for (int c = 0; c < k; ++c) {
                if (c >= 64 || (forbidden & (1ULL << c)) == 0) {
                    color[v] = c;
                    if (self(self, pos + 1)) return true;
                    color[v] = -1;
                }
            }
            return false;
        };
        
        success = solve(solve, 0);
    }
    
    // Assign default if still uncolored (may not be valid but ensures completeness)
    for (int i = 0; i < n; ++i) {
        if (color[i] == -1) {
            color[i] = 0;
        }
    }
    
    // Output
    for (int i = 0; i < n; ++i) {
        if (i > 0) std::cout << " ";
        std::cout << color[i];
    }
    std::cout << "\n";
    
    return 0;
}

use std::io;

fn main() {
    let mut input = String::new();
    io::stdin().read_to_string(&mut input).expect("Failed to read input");
    let mut tokens = input.split_whitespace();
    let n: usize = tokens.next().expect("No n").parse().expect("Parse n failed");
    let m: usize = tokens.next().expect("No m").parse().expect("Parse m failed");
    let mut used = vec![false; n];
    let mut cover: Vec<usize> = Vec::new();
    for _ in 0..m {
        let u_str = tokens.next().expect("No u");
        let v_str = tokens.next().expect("No v");
        let u: usize = u_str.parse().expect("Parse u failed");
        let v: usize = v_str.parse().expect("Parse v failed");
        if u < n && v < n && !used[u] && !used[v] {
            used[u] = true;
            used[v] = true;
            cover.push(u);
            cover.push(v);
        }
    }
    println!("{}", cover.len());
    if !cover.is_empty() {
        let mut output = String::with_capacity(cover.len() * 10);
        output.push_str(&cover[0].to_string());
        for &v in &cover[1..] {
            output.push(' ');
            output.push_str(&v.to_string());
        }
        println!("{}", output);
    } else {
        println!();
    }
}

You are writing C# code to solve the Maximum Clique problem, which is NP Hard.

Your C# maximum clique finder will be tested with graphs ranging from sparse to very dense instances.
The same algorithm must work efficiently across ALL graph complexities, from 20 vertices to 1 million.

**Problem:**
Find the largest complete subgraph (clique) in an undirected graph.
A clique is a set of vertices where every pair of vertices is connected by an edge.

**Input format (stdin):**
```
num_vertices num_edges
u v (for each edge, 0-indexed)
```

**Output format (stdout):**
```
clique_size
vertex_1 vertex_2 ... vertex_k (vertices in the maximum clique, space-separated)
```

**Success Criteria:**
- All vertices in output form a complete subgraph
- No larger clique exists in the graph
- Output format is correct

**Failure Criteria:**
- Output vertices don't form a clique
- Larger clique exists
- Timeout without solution
- Invalid output format
